summary: The added Scaladoc has several material exception omissions and incorrectly describes equality of composite `Equiv` instances as identity-based.

items.issue: The new throws documentation mentions a null `bd` but omits that a null `mc` also causes `bd.round(mc)` to throw `NullPointerException`.
items.suggestion: Document null `mc` as an additional `NullPointerException` condition.

items.issue: The newly documented arithmetic methods omit material `ArithmeticException` cases delegated to `java.math.BigDecimal`, including division by zero; division can also fail when the supplied `MathContext` cannot represent the requested result without permitted rounding.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws ArithmeticException` tags covering zero divisors and the applicable precision/rounding failures for each operation (or refer to the delegated Java operation precisely).

items.issue: These methods now selectively document null failures but omit the `ArithmeticException` thrown by their delegated `java.math.BigDecimal` operations when rounding is necessary while the context uses `UNNECESSARY`.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws ArithmeticException` tag for inexact results requiring rounding under `UNNECESSARY` (where applicable).

items.issue: The added return descriptions say the underlying `Equiv` instance(s) must be “the same,” implying reference identity. The implementations compare them with `==`, so distinct but equal `Equiv` instances make these objects equal.
items.suggestion: Say that the underlying `Equiv` instance(s) are equal (according to `==`), not that they are the same instance(s).

items.issue: The `@return` repeats the preceding sentence, which already begins with “Returns” and states the complete result.
Each `@return` restates its preceding “Returns” sentence without adding an edge case or other information.
